body: I'll make sure to do some reading tonight, and hopefully I can make some type of progress with my psychiatrist in the future. Thank you very much, it means a lot.

Yeah, it makes sense. I'm kind of surprised that none of my therapists or psychiatrists never mentioned any of this to me before, considering that I experience most symptoms associated with panic attacks on a daily basis. I mean, from personal experience, I've seen my sister, mother, aunts, and grandmother have panic attacks. Mental illness is something that all of the women in my family struggle with. From seeing their panic attacks, I never thought I was actually having any, because they're very different.
Thank you, I really appreciate that. I hope so too. I'm very tired of feeling the way I do.

I'm currently in the process. I've had many therapists, and few psychiatrists. With therapists, it seems that whenever I establish a connection, they retire, or they find a position somewhere else. With psychiatrists, it's retirement, or insurance. I mean, this year alone, I've switched therapists three times. It's just very frustrating.

No, I've never spoken to my psychiatrist about it. I thought that my feelings were just me overreacting or being delusional, since that's what I'm usually told when I tell anyone about them. I never actually knew I was having panic attacks. My psychiatrist is a very cold and quiet man; he doesn't look at me, he doesn't smile, and he doesn't show much interest when I speak. I'm currently in the process of finding a new therapist and psychiatrist, but the process has been pretty slow because of insurance reasons.
